items.title: Catherine of Aragon's Bedchamber Servant | Get Ready with Me
items.description:
Catalina of Motril was a former servant to Katherine of Aragon, first wife of Henry VIII. Likely enslaved, she was brought to England at the age of 15 to serve as a servant of the queen's bedchamber. 

In this video, historian Lauren Johnson and historical interpreter Safia Lamrani discuss the sources we have for what Catalina might have worn when she walked the halls of Tudor palaces like Hampton Court. Layer by layer, they build an outfit for a working woman at the Tudor court, with nods to Ca

items.title: Going Boldly: Space Shuttle Enterprise
items.channel_title: The History Guy: History Deserves to Be Remembered
items.description:
On August 12, 1977 the space shuttle Enterprise made its first free flight. That is, it was detached from its Boeing 747 "Shuttle Carrier Aircraft” and let fly. It is difficult to wrap my mind around the fact that this vehicle that once was, to me, the symbol of the future is now, itself, history. That is, perhaps, as ironic as the fact that the First Space Shuttle, Enterprise, never went to space.

global_silver_linings.snippet: A manatee is swimming free again thanks to a fishing guide who reported the animal tangled in crab trap lines, and the Georgia and Florida wildlife experts who raced to the scene. The drama played out over two days last week on the Mackay and Hampton rivers off St. Simons Island.
global_silver_linings.reason: A quick-thinking fishing guide's call for help meant a entangled manatee was freed while her calf looked on — a small act of compassion with a living, breathing outcome. It's a reminder that ordinary people paying attention can make an extraordinary difference for wildlife.
